ra: Simeon the Just opens the chain of transmission in Pirkei Avot, counted among the Sages.
Honi the Circle-Drawer is a charismatic sage attested in the Mishnah and Josephus.
Hillel the Elder is a foundational Tannaitic sage.
Shammai is a foundational Tannaitic sage and counterpart of Hillel.
Yohanan ben Zakkai is a leading post-Temple sage.
Akiva ben Joseph is a pre-eminent Tannaitic sage.
Judah ha-Nasi redacted the Mishnah, closing the Tannaitic chain of sages.
The Teacher of Righteousness is an inspired sectarian teacher of Second Temple Judaism, grouped with the era's learned leaders.
The House of Shammai (strict) and House of Hillel (lenient) are the paradigmatic Tannaitic halakhic dispute.
Reciprocal: Hillel's lenient school is opposed by Shammai's strict school in the Mishnah.
Akiva belongs to the generation of disciples following Yohanan ben Zakkai's Yavneh academy; lineage attested in rabbinic tradition but indirect.
Judah ha-Nasi's Mishnah is built on the halakhic systematization of Akiva (via Akiva's disciples), the dominant Tannaitic lineage.
Gamaliel the Elder (already in the DB as the Acts figure) is a leading Tannaitic sage, grandson of Hillel; cross-linking the existing entity into the Second Temple sages hub.
Gamaliel the Elder is traditionally Hillel's grandson and heir of the House of Hillel.
The Qumran pesharim depict the Wicked Priest persecuting the Teacher of Righteousness.
Reciprocal: the Wicked Priest is the persecutor of the Teacher of Righteousness in the Dead Sea Scrolls.
Josephus identifies as a Pharisee and learned interpreter of the Law; grouped with the era's learned figures (historian).
Judith is the protagonist of the deuterocanonical Book of Judith.
Holofernes is the antagonist of the Book of Judith.
Judith beheads the Assyrian general Holofernes to save Bethulia.
Reciprocal: Holofernes is slain by Judith.
Judas Maccabeus is the central figure of 1-2 Maccabees.
Judas is one of the five Maccabee brothers, sons of Mattathias.
The Maccabee brothers are deuterocanonical narrative figures of 1 Maccabees.
The Maccabee brothers lead the revolt against the persecuting Seleucid king Antiochus IV.
Antiochus IV Epiphanes is the chief antagonist of 1-2 Maccabees.
Antiochus IV is opposed by Judas Maccabeus, who rededicates the desecrated Temple.
The Maccabean mother is a martyr figure of 2 Maccabees 7.
The mother and her seven sons are martyred under Antiochus IV in 2 Maccabees 7.
Eleazar the scribe is the exemplary martyr of 2 Maccabees 6.
Eleazar is martyred under the persecution of Antiochus IV.
Tobias is the protagonist of the Book of Tobit.
Tobias is the son of Tobit (existing entity ENT_TOBIT) in the Book of Tobit.
Reciprocal: Tobit is the father of Tobias; wiring the existing ENT_TOBIT into the cohort.
Sarah of Tobit is a narrative figure of the Book of Tobit.
Sarah marries Tobias after being freed from the demon Asmodeus.
Reciprocal: Tobias marries Sarah in the Book of Tobit.
Tobias is guided on his journey by the disguised archangel Raphael (existing ENT_ISR_RAPHAEL) in the Book of Tobit.
Raphael binds the demon Asmodeus and frees Sarah, enabling her marriage (Book of Tobit).
Ahikar appears as Tobit's nephew within the Book of Tobit's deuterocanonical narrative.
Susanna is the heroine of the deuterocanonical addition to Daniel.
